_purpose: Pre-existing violations of a HARD TECHNOLOGY gate that are accepted for now, each with an owner, a dated expiry, and the action that clears it. Read by scripts/lib/gate_baseline.py.
_why: IMP-0439. Improvement review 36 built scripts/verify-provisioning-test-presence.py, measured it correctly (3 findings, all true), and wired it as step 4 of 72 in a build config where NO step declares a severity — so a non-zero exit halts the build. The gate was right and the next build was dead, over three provisioning scripts that predated the dispatch and which C-COM-002 says are not the introducing dispatch's to fix. IMP-0320 is the recorded correct handling of the same shape: build the gate, measure it, and where it is red over work the dispatch does not own, do not simply switch it on.
_not_a_waiver: An entry suppresses the FAIL, never the report. Every run still prints every finding with its baseline cited against it, the owner named and the expiry shown. An entry missing an owner, a reason, a clearing action or an expiry FAILS the gate. An EXPIRED entry FAILS. That is what stops a baseline becoming a permanent waiver — the same semantics contract/known-exceptions.json already uses for the commercial gates.
_not_coverage_exclusions: This is NOT config/coverage-exclusions.json and the two must not be conflated. That file carves out the C-TECH-014 line-coverage threshold and requires a `proven_able_to_fail` per entry, which a script with no tests at all cannot supply; it is also capped at 6 entries with 4 used. Adding these three there would have breached the cap with the wrong instrument.
_decision: Taken by the reviewer (Xander Lykopoulos) under APPROVE IMPROVEMENTS, 2026-08-28, on improvement review 37 section 7. The reviewer named lead-agent as owner rather than themselves, on the ground that an untested provisioning script is a system/process item rather than a delivery one, and set the expiry at 2026-09-30 — the date contract/known-exceptions.json's EX-002 uses for work that is in our own hands and needs no re-approval.
_second_gate_added_2026_08_28: Improvement review 38 added the `tad-coverage` entries below, under the same keyword and by the same rule. Its new assertion (e) — every status value the system produces appears in the response contract's enumeration — measured 2 findings, both TRUE, against a document (docs/architecture/trustee-portal-visual-refresh-architecture.md section 3.3) owned by architect-agent, whose concurrent dispatch corrected Appendix A in the same hour and did NOT widen this enumeration. The reviewer chose the baseline over holding the wiring, so all three new assertions ship HARD today and the one red assertion carries a date instead of a switch. Note the shape is IMP-0439's exactly: a correct gate, red over work the introducing dispatch does not own.
_four_not_three: The approval named THREE scripts and this file carries FOUR. The fourth, create-self-signed-cert.ps1, is the direct and measured consequence of change 6 of the same review, which the same keyword approved: excluding the convention suite from counting as coverage evidence moves the gate's true-positive set from 3 to 4, and that measurement is in review 37 section 6c, in front of the reviewer at approval. Applying change 6 without this entry would leave the build red, which is the exact outcome change 7 and decision 2 exist to prevent. Recorded here, in the entry's applied_by, and in the gate output rather than made silently — improvement-agent.md's NARROW-AND-REPORT rule. Same owner, same expiry, same class as the other three.
_status_pending_removed_2026_08_30: Improvement review 43 change 2 REPLACED the `status:pending` entry with `status-unproduced:threshold-unset`. This is a removal, not a re-decision, and it is recorded rather than done silently. Change 2 split assertion (e) into two directions and asks the undeclared-producer question of the FLOW set alone, because the response contract's enumeration describes the response BODY and `pending` is an app-in-flight state that never travels in one. So `pending` now leaves BY CONSTRUCTION and its key can never be claimed again. An unclaimable entry is not harmless here: load_baselines FAILS on any expired entry for the gate whether or not it was ever claimed — verified by running it against 2026-10-01 — so leaving it would have turned the build red on 2026-10-01 over a finding that can no longer occur. The reviewer's 2026-08-28 decision that pending is real and correct is unchanged; only the instrument that was excusing it is gone, because there is nothing left to excuse.
_owner_of_status_error_unchanged: The `status:error` entry below keeps owner lead-agent, set by the reviewer on 2026-08-28. Review 43 described both directions as architect-agent's; only the NEW entry carries that owner. Rewriting a recorded decision on an existing entry was deliberately not done.

baselines.reason: The PRD Dataverse APPLICATION USER for $PROVISION_APP_ID does not exist, and cannot be created by this repository: it needs System Administrator on the production environment, and more fundamentally the provisioning identity lacks the Entra ID admin consent that only a tenant Global Administrator can grant. The reviewer has been performing these PRD operations MANUALLY, as an administrator, rather than through the service principal. Reviewer's own words, 2026-09-03: "I did those actions myself because we couldn't get the permissions right without a global administrator approving the permission in EntraID. Don't throw these away, park these for now." Same root as IMP-0105, which established that a successful Graph connection proves the credential and never the permission. By extension this covers the six PRD provisioning steps behind the note — bind-roles-to-groups.ps1, ensure-column-security-profile-members.ps1, ensure-auditing.ps1, ensure-bulk-delete-jobs.ps1, seed-settings.ps1, share-apps.ps1, all -Env prd — which is why it is PARKED rather than dropped: they remain the pipeline's declared shape, performed by a named human today.
baselines.clears_when: A tenant Global Administrator grants admin consent for $PROVISION_APP_ID against the PRD environment, AND a Dataverse application user for that app id exists in PRD holding the same security role it holds in DEV, proven by `pwsh provisioning/dataverse/verify-environment-access.ps1 -Env prd` exiting 0 with a live WhoAmI. THIS IS AN EXTERNAL APPROVAL, NOT A CALENDAR EVENT: it is not scheduled and it is not in this project's gift, which is the reviewer's stated reason for parking rather than dating the underlying note. Then delete this entry — do not re-date it. Until it holds, the six -Env prd provisioning steps stay in the config as the declared shape and are executed by the reviewer as an administrator, which is a recorded manual route, not a gap.
baselines.expiry_rationale: NOT a prediction of when consent arrives — nobody here controls that. It is the date by which the ACCEPTANCE must be retaken, and it is deliberately the same date EX-001, EX-003 and EX-005 use in contract/known-exceptions.json: Phase 3's contractual milestone, the point past which PRD matters for real. An exception blocked on an external approval is the kind most likely to be forgotten, so it must not outlive the phase that needs it. The reviewer may shorten this; nothing depends on the length except how long it can be ignored.
baselines._not_in_known_exceptions_json: Recorded HERE and deliberately not also as an EX-nnn in contract/known-exceptions.json. That file's own _gate_scope_note records technology entries as the anomaly (EX-004 was the first and C-COM-010's wording was never widened to match), and THIS file was purpose-built for technology gates. One record, one owner, one expiry: duplicating it across both files gives the same decision two expiry dates that can drift apart, and the reviewer's requirement was that it not vanish from verify-pipeline-config.py's view — which an entry here satisfies directly, because that gate now reads this file on every run.

_sixth_gate_added_2026_09_03: Improvement review 2026-09-03 (IMP-0588) opted scripts/verify-pipeline-config.py into this file as the gate key 'pipeline-config', for the PRD application-user note below. The shape is IMP-0439's again — a correct gate, red over work this project does not own — but the blocker here is EXTERNAL: Entra ID admin consent for $PROVISION_APP_ID that only a tenant Global Administrator can grant, and which has not been granted. Note WHY a baseline and not a re-date: re-dating a blocked_on asserts 'I re-tested it today and it is still blocked', which is false when nobody re-tested it, and the 14-day window then hides the note completely until it expires again. The reviewer refused that silent vanish by name. Leaving it a hard error was the other wrong answer: pipeline-config-preflight validates the WHOLE file, so one PRD note halts every DEV build of every feature at step 2 of 72. The note keeps its original 2026-08-19 date and stays permanently expired — telling the truth — and this entry carries the owner, the clearing action and the re-decision deadline.
